transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been getting really bothered by how my face looks lately. We put in a brighter bathroom mirror, and ever since then I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven or kind of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, but I keep seeing it.
Do you find yourself thinking about your face a lot throughout the day?

Yes, I do. It’s been on my mind a lot since we got that brighter mirror. I keep looking at my cheeks and jaw and thinking the skin looks uneven or kind of saggy, even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
Has worrying about your face affected your daily activities or relationships in any way?

A little, yes. I still get my work done, but I’ve been spending extra time getting ready, so a few mornings I’ve ended up rushing into the courthouse. I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once too. And I’ve skipped being in some casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to worry about how my face would look.
Have you been doing anything repeatedly to try and fix or check your face?

Yes. Most mornings I check my face in the mirror from a few different angles, especially around my cheeks and jaw. Then I usually put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse. I also catch myself comparing my face to women I see at work, and if I’m not feeling okay about how I look, I’ll avoid being in casual pictures.
Is it always your face, specifically your cheeks and jaw, that you're concerned about, or have you worried about other parts of your body as well?

It’s really been my face, mainly the cheeks and jaw area. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin there and thinking it looks uneven or a little saggy. I haven’t really been focused on other parts of my body in the same way.
Do you feel like you have to check your face in the mirror a certain number of times or in a specific way?

Not a certain number, no. It’s more that most mornings I end up looking from a few different angles, especially before I leave for the courthouse. If I don’t feel okay about it, I’ll put on a little extra makeup. And later I might catch myself comparing my face to women at work, but it’s not like I have a set routine I have to do exactly.
Do you think your face would look normal if the skin around your cheeks and jaw were perfectly even and not saggy?

Yes, I think that’s what bothers me. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep seeing the skin around my cheeks and jaw as uneven or kind of saggy. If it looked smooth and firm, I think I’d feel like my face looked normal. My husband says he can’t really see what I mean, but I still notice it.
Do you think you would stop worrying about your appearance if the skin around your cheeks and jaw looked exactly as you want it to?

I think so, yes. If that skin around my cheeks and jaw looked even and not saggy, I don’t think I’d be so focused on it. That’s really what I keep noticing in the brighter mirror, even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
Is there something specific that you think is wrong with the appearance of your cheeks and jaw that you're trying to fix?

Yes. It’s mainly that the skin around my cheeks and along my jaw looks uneven to me, and kind of saggy. I started noticing it a lot more after we put in that brighter bathroom mirror. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but I do, and that’s what I keep wanting to fix.
Is it always the unevenness and sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw that bothers you, or have you had concerns about other specific flaws in your face?

It’s really just that area, the skin around my cheeks and jaw. Since we got that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep seeing it as uneven or a little saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really see what I mean, but that’s what I keep noticing.
Is there something specific that you think would need to change about the appearance of your cheeks and jaw for you to stop worrying about them?

I guess it would need to look smoother and more even, not like it’s sagging around my cheeks and jaw. That’s the thing I keep seeing, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror, even though my husband says he can’t really see what I mean.
Is your concern about your face focused on this one issue with your cheeks and jaw, or do you think there might be other flaws that could bother you just as much if this one were fixed?

It’s really focused on the cheeks and jaw. I’m not sitting there picking apart my whole face—just that uneven, sort of saggy look I notice there, especially since we got that brighter bathroom mirror. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but it keeps standing out to me.
Do you think other people can see the unevenness and sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw, or is it something that only you can notice?

I think it might mostly be me noticing it. I mean, to me it looks uneven and kind of saggy, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror, but my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about. So I’m not sure other people see it the way I do.
Do you feel like your worries about your face are significantly interfering with your overall happiness or well-being?

Yes, somewhat. I mean, I still get my work done and I’m functioning, but it does get in the way. I spend extra time getting ready, and that’s made me rush into the courthouse late a few mornings. I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because of it. And I’ve skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to worry about how my face would look.
Do you think your perception of your face is different from how it actually looks?

Yes, I think it probably is. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep seeing the skin around my cheeks and jaw as uneven or kind of saggy. But my husband says he really doesn’t see what I’m talking about, so I guess my perception may be harsher than how it actually looks.
Do you think your face actually looks uneven and saggy, or is it just that you feel like it should look better?

I think it actually looks that way to me, especially since we got that brighter bathroom mirror. I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy. But then my husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so I guess part of me knows it may just be how I’m seeing it.
Do you think you would worry about your face if you couldn't see the skin around your cheeks and jaw at all?

Probably not as much. I mean, that’s really what sets it off for me—seeing that area in the brighter bathroom mirror. Once I notice my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or saggy, then I start worrying about it. If I couldn’t see that part at all, I don’t think I’d focus on it the same way.
Do you think your view of your face is realistic?

I’m not sure it’s completely realistic. To me, in that brighter bathroom mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw really does look uneven or saggy. But my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, so I guess I know my view might be more negative than how it actually looks.
Is there something specific about the appearance of your cheeks and jaw that you think is abnormal or unattractive?

Yes. It’s mainly the skin around my cheeks and jaw. In that brighter bathroom mirror, it looks uneven to me, and kind of saggy. That’s what feels unattractive or not normal to me, even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
